Offing

Offing finds the runtimes, packages, and GitHub Actions in a repository that are already end-of-life or deprecated, shows the exact file and line, and backs every finding with an authoritative source, a replacement, and migration steps — locally, offline, and with no account.

Read this in: English · فارسی.

npx @velella/offing scan .

For coding agents, install the Agent Skill with one command. It teaches your agent to find, explain, and migrate these findings, and it is listed on skills.sh:

npx skills add velella-sh/offing

Node.js 22 or newer. Start with Install (npm, Action, MCP, plugins, Docker, Homebrew), then the 90-second demo on a deliberately outdated project:

Found 5 lifecycle risks. The most urgent:
  HIGH Unsupported actions/checkout runtime (.github/workflows/ci.yml:9)
  MEDIUM Node.js 18 is end-of-life (package.json:5)
  MEDIUM Node.js 19 is end-of-life (package.json:5)
  …and 2 more below.

Try it

  • Install: one page for every channel — npm, Action, MCP, plugins, Docker, and Homebrew.
  • Five-step quickstart: from the first scan to a baseline in CI.
  • 90-second demo: a deliberately outdated project, scanned, explained, and turned into migration context.
  • CLI reference: every command, flag, shell completion, and exit code.
  • Playbook: manual CLI checks: scan, read, decide, accept, and keep findings from returning.
  • Runtime drift: every runtime version a repository states, and whether they agree.
  • Upgrade check: whether a project can move to a target runtime, with each blocker and its evidence.
  • Local MCP server: the tools and output schemas an agent can call.
  • Environment doctor and compatibility: supported ecosystems, hosts, and maturity.

Set up CI

  • GitHub Action: pull request comments, SARIF code scanning, and severity gates.
  • Playbook: GitHub Actions: add the Action, read what it reports, and accept findings on purpose.
  • GitLab CI/CD component: the component, its permissions, and self-managed constraints.
  • Playbook: GitLab pipelines: gate merges on severity and accept known findings.
  • Organization rollout: scan every repository with one reusable workflow and a weekly digest.
  • Hooks: scan before every push, or block a deprecated package install in an agent.
  • Privacy: what stays on your machine and the one command that uses the network.

Use with agents

  • Agent Skill: the portable skill for coding agents and how its triggering is evaluated.
  • Playbook: agent-driven migrations: migrate one finding while Offing supplies the facts and the proof.
  • Migration packets: the structured context Offing builds for one finding.
  • Migration plans: waves of independent migration tasks for parallel agent sessions.
  • Capability manifest: how a tool or agent discovers what Offing can do.
  • Claude plugin: install Offing, its Skill, and the dependency guard in Claude Code.
  • Codex plugin: install Offing and the dependency guard in Codex.
  • Codex and Claude plugin packaging: how the plugins are built and published.
  • Cross-host plugin evaluation and security boundaries: what each host can and cannot enforce.

Reference

  • Benchmarks: the agent migration benchmark, its task set, and how it is scored.
  • State of EOL: corpus findings aggregated by product and release line.
  • Offing compared with Renovate, Dependabot, and endoflife.date: what each tool answers, and where each is stronger.
  • Decision records: the decisions behind public contracts.
  • Roadmap: phases and what each one delivers.
  • Post-launch notes and next roadmap: what shipped after v0.1 and what comes next.
  • Changelog: every release, with a stable link per version.
  • Start contributing: pick a sized issue, follow its brief, and open one pull request.
  • Codex plugin submission: how the plugin is submitted to the Codex directory.
  • Brand guide, brand asset terms, and the distribution brand checklist.
  • Support and terms.
